## Data

The data comes from the
[Iris dataset included in scikit-learn](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.datasets.load_iris.html).

## Load and inspect the data

```{python}
#| echo: true

from sklearn.datasets import load_iris
import pandas as pd

iris = load_iris(as_frame=True)
df = iris.frame

df.head()
```

The dataset contains measurements of iris flowers, including sepal length,
sepal width, petal length, and petal width.

## Average measurements by species

```{python}
#| echo: true

df.groupby("target").mean()
```

The three species have noticeably different average measurements.
In particular, petal length and petal width increase substantially across
the three target groups.

## Compare petal length across species

```{python}
#| echo: true

df.groupby("target")["petal length (cm)"].agg(["mean", "min", "max"])
```

The target groups have clearly different ranges of petal length, suggesting
that petal length may be useful for distinguishing between iris species.

## Sepal length versus petal length

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| label: fig-iris-scatter
#| fig-cap: "Relationship between sepal length and petal length in the Iris dataset."

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

plt.scatter(
    df["sepal length (cm)"],
    df["petal length (cm)"]
)

plt.xlabel("Sepal length (cm)")
plt.ylabel("Petal length (cm)")
plt.show()
```

The scatter plot shows a positive relationship between sepal length and
petal length: flowers with longer sepals generally also have longer petals.
